literal: An edict entrusted him to the Ministry of State Affairs; on examination he was rated clear, fair, diligent, and capable, and was forwarded to the Ministry of Personnel.
idiomatic: An edict placed him in the hands of the Ministry of State Affairs; when they examined his record they found him clear, fair, diligent, and capable, and sent him on to the Ministry of Personnel.

literal: In the seventh year an edict ordered the collation of the collected classics to supply the Crown Prince.
idiomatic: In the seventh year an edict ordered the collation of the collected classics for the Crown Prince's use.

literal: Xun, together with eleven others—the Jizhou licentiate Gao Qianhe, the Yingzhou licentiate Ma Jingde, Xu San'chou, Han Tongbao, the Luozhou licentiate Fu Huai'de, the Huaizhou licentiate Gu Daozi, the Guangping commandery filial exemplar Li Hanzi, the Bohai commandery filial exemplar Bao Changxuan, the Yangping commandery filial exemplar Jing Sun, the former Liangzhou establishment chief clerk Wang Jiuyuan, and the former establishment water-bureau section chief Zhou Zishen—were alike summoned by the Ministry to collate together.
idiomatic: Xun and eleven others—the Jizhou licentiate Gao Qianhe, the Yingzhou licentiate Ma Jingde, Xu San'chou, Han Tongbao, the Luozhou licentiate Fu Huai'de, the Huaizhou licentiate Gu Daozi, the Guangping filial exemplar Li Hanzi, the Bohai filial exemplar Bao Changxuan, the Yangping filial exemplar Jing Sun, the former Liangzhou establishment chief clerk Wang Jiuyuan, and the former establishment water-bureau section chief Zhou Zishen—were summoned by the Ministry to collate as one body.

literal: At that time many books in the secret repository were corrupt; Xun then proposed: "According to the precedent of Liu Xiang, Director of the Fortress at Hanzhong, who received an imperial charge to collate books—whenever he finished a single work he would memorialize the throne, always stating: 'Your servant Xiang's copy, Director of the Long Water Gate Your servant Can's copy, the Grand Historian's copy, the Grand Director of Ceremonies doctor's copy, inner and outer office copies—so many fascicles in all were compared and collated, and only then was the final text fixed in ink.'"
idiomatic: Many volumes in the secret repository were corrupt at the time, and Xun proposed: "We should follow Liu Xiang, Director of the Fortress at Hanzhong, who received an imperial charge to collate the classics. Whenever he finished a book he would memorialize the throne, always reporting: 'Your servant Xiang's copy, Director of the Long Water Gate Your servant Can's copy, the Grand Historian's copy, the Grand Director of Ceremonies doctor's copy, and inner and outer office copies—so many fascicles in all were compared and collated, and only then was the text fixed in ink for publication.'"

literal: The collations now under review were intended for the weightiest use, issued from the Orchid Terrace and kept in the First-Rank Archives.
idiomatic: The texts we are collating now are meant for the gravest purposes, issued from the Orchid Terrace and housed in the First-Rank Archives.

literal: Liu Xiang's precedent survives in the office archives; to collate and fix texts now, one must rely on many copies.
idiomatic: Liu Xiang's procedure still survives in the office archives; if we mean to collate and fix the texts now, we must lean on many copies.

literal: Grand Director of Ceremonies Xing Zicai, Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince Wei Shou, Minister of Personnel Xin Shu, Vice Minister of Revenue Mu Zirong, former Yellow Gate Gentleman Sima Zirui, and the late Director of the Imperial University Li Yexing were all houses rich in books; he asked that lists be sent to borrow their copies for collating gains and losses.
idiomatic: Grand Director of Ceremonies Xing Zicai, Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince Wei Shou, Minister of Personnel Xin Shu, Vice Minister of Revenue Mu Zirong, former Yellow Gate Gentleman Sima Zirui, and the late Director of the Imperial University Li Yexing all kept great libraries; he asked that lists be sent so their copies might be borrowed to collate against our texts.

literal: Secretariat Supervisor Wei Jin forwarded the matter to the chief seat of the Ministry; in all they obtained more than three thousand juan of alternate copies, and among the Five Classics and the various histories scarcely anything was left out.
idiomatic: Secretariat Supervisor Wei Jin forwarded the request to the Ministry's chief seat; in all they obtained more than three thousand juan of alternate copies, and among the Five Classics and the various histories scarcely a title was missing.

literal: In the eighth year an edict opened selection for officials of the Eastern and Western Provinces at the Ministry; in the policy questions set by the office, Xun ranked first in his day.
idiomatic: In the eighth year an edict opened selection for officials of the Eastern and Western Provinces at the Ministry; in the policy questions set by the office, Xun took first place in his generation.

literal: Left Vice Director Yang Yin recruited Xun as a staff officer in his establishment.
idiomatic: Left Vice Director Yang Yin recruited Xun as a staff officer in his establishment.

literal: Xun declined, saying: "My clan is poor and mean; if I seek a ranked post I am sure to fail. I beg to be appointed an irregular aide who supervises the establishment's military affairs."
idiomatic: Xun declined, saying, "My house is poor and low; if I seek a ranked post I am sure to fail. I beg instead for an irregular aide who supervises the establishment's military affairs."

literal: Yin said: "When talent is high, one does not follow the usual rule."
idiomatic: Yin said, "When talent runs high, one does not follow the usual rule."

literal: He memorialized specially to employ him.
idiomatic: He memorialized specially to employ him.

literal: In the ninth year an edict promoted him by exception to irregular general.
idiomatic: In the ninth year an edict promoted him by exception to irregular general.

literal: Later, when Shizu was stationed at Ye, he was summoned into the Secretariat to manage documents.
idiomatic: Later, when Shizu was stationed at Ye, he was summoned into the Secretariat to manage documents.

literal: When Shizu ascended the throne, he was transferred and made chief secretary, then promoted to irregular attendant of the cavalry.
idiomatic: When Shizu ascended the throne, he was transferred and made chief secretary, then promoted to irregular attendant of the cavalry.

literal: At the start of Tiantong he died of illness.
idiomatic: At the opening of Tiantong he died of illness.

literal: Liu Ti, styled Zichang, was a man of Congting Lane in Pengcheng.
idiomatic: Liu Ti, styled Zichang, came from Congting Lane in Pengcheng.

literal: His grandfather Fang was Grand Director of Ceremonies of Wei.
idiomatic: His grandfather Fang had been Grand Director of Ceremonies of Wei.

literal: His father Yi was a Grand Master of Splendid Virtue with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
idiomatic: His father Yi held the rank of Grand Master of Splendid Virtue with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

literal: Ti was clever from youth, fond of hunting and archery on horseback, taking pleasure in travel as his business, loving company, and skilled at jest.
idiomatic: Ti was clever from youth, fond of hunting and archery on horseback; he made pleasure and travel his trade, loved company, and was skilled at jest.

literal: The commandery recruited him as merit officer; the province appointed him chief clerk.
idiomatic: The commandery recruited him as merit officer; the province appointed him chief clerk.

literal: At the end of Wei he was summoned to the hegemon's office; Shizong made him a traveling aide in the establishment of Prince of Yong'an Jun.
idiomatic: At the end of Wei he was summoned to the hegemon's office; Shizong made him a traveling aide in the establishment of Prince of Yong'an Jun.

literal: Far from his home district and weary of life on the road, he roused himself in anger and applied himself solely to reading.
idiomatic: Far from home and weary of life on the road, he roused himself and bent all his force to reading.

literal: Jinyang was the gathering place of the hegemon's court; men of the ruling house flocked there, all bent on feasting.
idiomatic: Jinyang was the gathering place of the hegemon's court; men of the ruling house flocked there, all bent on feasting.

literal: Even amid these revels Ti never let his scroll leave his hand; whenever he came upon a text he had not seen before, he would chant it through the day, sometimes not returning home all night—such was his love of learning.
idiomatic: Even amid these revels Ti never let his scroll leave his hand; whenever he came upon a text he had not seen before, he would chant it through the day, sometimes not returning home all night—such was his hunger for learning.

literal: He also turned his mind to belles-lettres and was quite skilled at verse.
idiomatic: He also turned his mind to belles-lettres and was quite skilled at verse.

literal: At the start of Tianbao he served as acting magistrate of Dingtao county and was dismissed on a charge of misconduct; for more than ten years he received no new appointment.
idiomatic: At the opening of Tianbao he served as acting magistrate of Dingtao county and was dismissed on a charge of misconduct; for more than ten years he received no new appointment.

literal: In the Qianming era he was concurrently irregular attendant of the cavalry and sent as envoy to Liang's ruler Xiao Zhuang; on his return he was concurrently a gentleman of the Three Excellencies Bureau.
idiomatic: In the Qianming era he was concurrently irregular attendant of the cavalry and sent as envoy to Liang's ruler Xiao Zhuang; on his return he was concurrently a gentleman of the Three Excellencies Bureau.

literal: In the first year of Huangjian he was made mentor of the heir.
idiomatic: In the first year of Huangjian he was made mentor of the heir.

literal: When Suzong died, he followed Shizu to Jinyang, was made irregular attendant of the cavalry, and concurrently a gentleman of the Ceremonies Bureau.
idiomatic: When Suzong died, he followed Shizu to Jinyang, was made irregular attendant of the cavalry, and concurrently a gentleman of the Ceremonies Bureau.

literal: After a long while he was concurrently a gentleman of the Secretariat.
idiomatic: After a long while he was concurrently a gentleman of the Secretariat.

literal: He Shikai held favor and power; Ti attached himself to him, was formally appointed gentleman of the Secretariat, entered to manage secrets, was concurrently irregular attendant of the cavalry, and served as chief envoy to Chen.
idiomatic: He Shikai held favor and power; Ti attached himself to him, was formally appointed gentleman of the Secretariat, entered to manage secrets, was concurrently irregular attendant of the cavalry, and served as chief envoy to Chen.

literal: On his return he was made attendant of direct communication and irregular cavalry.
idiomatic: On his return he was made attendant of direct communication and irregular cavalry.

literal: Soon he was promoted to attendant who presents matters to the Yellow Gate, edited the national history, and was given concurrent irregular attendant of the cavalry.
idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to attendant who presents matters to the Yellow Gate, edited the national history, and was given concurrent irregular attendant of the cavalry.

literal: He was further made acting insignia equal to the Three Excellencies and deputy chief envoy to Zhou.
idiomatic: He was further made acting insignia equal to the Three Excellencies and deputy chief envoy to Zhou.

literal: When the two states first opened relations, ritual had not yet been fixed; Ti debated back and forth with the Zhou court, weighing past and present, and in most matters matched ritual; his literary phrasing was also admirable, and he won great reputation.
idiomatic: When the two states first opened relations, ritual had not yet been fixed; Ti debated back and forth with the Zhou court, weighing past and present, and in most matters matched ritual; his literary phrasing was also admirable, and he won great reputation.

literal: When the mission returned, he was given insignia equal to the Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: When the mission returned, he was given insignia equal to the Three Excellencies.

literal: When Shizu died, he went out as inspector of Jiang province.
idiomatic: When Shizu died, he went out as inspector of Jiang province.

literal: When Zu Ting held power, he was moved to inspector of Ren province.
idiomatic: When Zu Ting held power, he was moved to inspector of Ren province.

literal: After Zu Ting was removed, Ti was recalled, kept on call at the Forest of Literature Hall, and again made irregular attendant of the cavalry to present matters at the Gate.
idiomatic: After Zu Ting was removed, Ti was recalled, kept on call at the Forest of Literature Hall, and again made irregular attendant of the cavalry to present matters at the Gate.

literal: Before long he was executed together with Cui Jishu and others at the same time, aged forty-nine.
idiomatic: Before long he was executed together with Cui Jishu and others at the same time, aged forty-nine.

literal: Earlier Ti and Zu Ting had found each other through literary affinity and made a bond like Lei and Chen; he also had his younger brother Jun take Ting's daughter in marriage.
idiomatic: Earlier Ti and Zu Ting had found each other through literary affinity and made a bond like Lei and Chen; he also had his younger brother Jun take Ting's daughter in marriage.

literal: When Ting was about to remove Zhao Yanshen and the others, he first told Ti and even handed him a secret memorial, ordering him to report it to the throne.
idiomatic: When Ting was about to remove Zhao Yanshen and the others, he first told Ti and even handed him a secret memorial, ordering him to report it to the throne.

literal: Yanshen and the others learned of it somewhat in advance and pleaded their own case first; because of this Ting suspected Ti had informed on what he had done.
idiomatic: Yanshen and the others learned of it somewhat in advance and pleaded their own case first; because of this Ting suspected Ti had informed on what he had done.

literal: When Ting was removed, Ti at once sent his brother to divorce her—so lightly did he break ties and cut relations.
idiomatic: When Ting was removed, Ti at once sent his brother to divorce her—so lightly did he break ties and cut relations.

literal: The poetry, rhapsodies, and miscellaneous prose he composed came to thirty juan.
idiomatic: The poetry, rhapsodies, and miscellaneous prose he composed came to thirty juan.

literal: His son Yimin was a traveling aide in an establishment office.
idiomatic: His son Yimin was a traveling aide in an establishment office.

literal: Ti's younger brother Cha was clever from youth and loved literature.
idiomatic: Ti's younger brother Cha was clever from youth and loved literature.

literal: Between Tiantong and Wuping he served in turn as attendant censor within the palace, concurrently irregular attendant of the cavalry, welcomed and entertained the Chen envoy, and was transferred to a gentleman of the Ceremonies Bureau in the Ministry.
idiomatic: Between Tiantong and Wuping he served in turn as attendant censor within the palace, concurrently irregular attendant of the cavalry, welcomed and entertained the Chen envoy, and was transferred to a gentleman of the Ceremonies Bureau in the Ministry.

literal: At the end of the Zhou era of Great Elephant he died as administrator of Li province.
idiomatic: At the end of the Zhou era of Great Elephant he died as administrator of Li province.

literal: His son Xuandao had character and judgment and served as cavalry section chief of Ding province.
idiomatic: His son Xuandao had character and judgment and served as cavalry section chief of Ding province.

literal: Ti's nephew Yan, styled Junqing.
idiomatic: Ti's nephew Yan, styled Junqing.

literal: His grandfather Yin was a minister of Wei and was killed by Gaozu.
idiomatic: His grandfather Yin had been a minister of Wei and was killed by Gaozu.

literal: Yan's father Ji and Ji's younger brother Jun both fled south of the Yangtze.
idiomatic: Yan's father Ji and Ji's younger brother Jun both fled south of the Yangtze.

literal: Yan was given out in adoption.
idiomatic: Yan was given out in adoption.

literal: In the Wuding era he followed Jun back north.
idiomatic: In the Wuding era he followed Jun back north.

literal: He was granted the title Marquis of Linying and died in the Daning era as a secretary in the Grand Marshal's office.
idiomatic: He was granted the title Marquis of Linying and died in the Daning era as a secretary in the Grand Marshal's office.

literal: Yan loved literature, was skilled at cursive script, and his bearing was very fine.
idiomatic: Yan loved literature, was skilled at cursive script, and his bearing was very fine.

literal: He served in turn as outer military section chief of Ying province and merit officer in the Ministry of Works, was kept on call at the Forest of Literature Hall, and was made direct judge in the Court of Review.
idiomatic: He served in turn as outer military section chief of Ying province and merit officer in the Ministry of Works, was kept on call at the Forest of Literature Hall, and was made direct judge in the Court of Review.

literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he was a secretary of Zheng province and died.
idiomatic: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he was a secretary of Zheng province and died.

literal: Yan Zhitui, styled Jie, was a man of Linyi in Langye.
idiomatic: Yan Zhitui, styled Jie, came from Linyi in Langye.

literal: His ninth-generation ancestor Han, following Emperor Yuan of Jin east across the river, reached the post of attendant, Right Grand Master of Splendid Virtue, and Marquis of Xiping.
idiomatic: His ninth-generation ancestor Han, following Emperor Yuan of Jin east across the river, reached the post of attendant, Right Grand Master of Splendid Virtue, and Marquis of Xiping.

literal: His father Xie was a consulting officer in the western establishment staff of Xiao Yi, Prince of Xiangdong.
idiomatic: His father Xie was a consulting officer in the western establishment staff of Xiao Yi, Prince of Xiangdong.

literal: The family had long excelled in the Offices of Zhou and the Zuo Tradition; Zhitui received the household learning early.
idiomatic: The family had long excelled in the Offices of Zhou and the Zuo Tradition; Zhitui received the household learning early.

literal: At twelve, when Yi was himself lecturing on the Zhuangzi and Laozi, he was admitted among the disciples.
idiomatic: At twelve, when Yi was himself lecturing on the Zhuangzi and Laozi, he was admitted among the disciples.

literal: Empty talk was not to his taste; he returned to the study of the Rites and the Commentaries, ranged widely through books, and was thorough in all he touched; his phrasing was classical and beautiful, and the western establishment praised him highly.
idiomatic: Empty talk was not to his taste; he returned to the study of the Rites and the Commentaries, ranged widely through books, and was thorough in all he touched; his phrasing was classical and beautiful, and the western establishment praised him highly.

literal: Yi made him regular attendant of the state on the left and added him as ink-and-brush section chief of the western establishment.
idiomatic: Yi made him regular attendant of the state on the left and added him as ink-and-brush section chief of the western establishment.

literal: He loved wine, was much given to license, and did not keep his dress in order; opinion at the time therefore thought less of him.
idiomatic: He loved wine, was much given to license, and did not keep his dress in order; opinion at the time therefore thought less of him.

literal: Yi sent the heir Fangzhu out to garrison Yingzhou and put Zhitui in charge of documents.
idiomatic: Yi sent the heir Fangzhu out to garrison Yingzhou and put Zhitui in charge of documents.

literal: When Hou Jing took Yingzhou he repeatedly wished to kill him; he was spared thanks to Wang Ze, a gentleman in Jing's traveling office.
idiomatic: When Hou Jing took Yingzhou he repeatedly wished to kill him; he was spared thanks to Wang Ze, a gentleman in Jing's traveling office.

literal: He was imprisoned and sent to Jiankang.
idiomatic: He was imprisoned and sent to Jiankang.

literal: When Jing was pacified, he returned to Jiangling.
idiomatic: When Jing was pacified, he returned to Jiangling.

literal: By then Yi had declared himself ruler; he made Zhitui irregular attendant of the cavalry and a gentleman who presents matters in the heir's household.
idiomatic: By then Yi had declared himself ruler; he made Zhitui irregular attendant of the cavalry and a gentleman who presents matters in the heir's household.

literal: Later he was defeated by the Zhou army.
idiomatic: Later he was defeated by the Zhou army.

literal: Grand General Li Xianqing valued him, recommended him to Hongnong, and had him manage the correspondence of his elder brother, the Duke of Yangping, Yuan.
idiomatic: Grand General Li Xianqing valued him, recommended him to Hongnong, and had him manage the correspondence of his elder brother, the Duke of Yangping, Yuan.

literal: When the river rose in sudden flood, he prepared a boat and came fleeing with wife and children; he passed the peril of the Rapids, and men of the time praised his courage and resolve.
idiomatic: When the river rose in sudden flood, he prepared a boat and came fleeing with wife and children; he passed the peril of the Rapids, and men of the time praised his courage and resolve.

literal: Xianzu saw him and was pleased, at once made him a court gentleman for attendance, brought him into the inner lodge to attend left and right, and favored him with frequent glances.
idiomatic: Xianzu saw him and was pleased, at once made him a court gentleman for attendance, brought him into the inner lodge to attend left and right, and favored him with frequent glances.

literal: At the end of Tianbao he followed the ruler to Heavenly Pool; he was made a secretary in the Secretariat and ordered that Secretariat Gentleman Duan Xiaoxin bring out the edict documents and show them to Zhitui.
idiomatic: At the end of Tianbao he followed the ruler to Heavenly Pool; he was made a secretary in the Secretariat and ordered that Secretariat Gentleman Duan Xiaoxin bring out the edict documents and show them to Zhitui.

literal: Zhitui was drinking outside the camp; when Xiaoxin returned and reported the matter, Xianzu said: "Let it wait."
idiomatic: Zhitui was drinking outside the camp; when Xiaoxin returned and reported the matter, Xianzu said, "Let it wait."

literal: Because of this the appointment was dropped.
idiomatic: Because of this the appointment was dropped.

literal: At the end of the Heqing era he was recommended as merit officer in Zhao province, soon kept on call at the Forest of Literature Hall, and made recording officer in the Grand Marshal's office.
idiomatic: At the end of the Heqing era he was recommended as merit officer in Zhao province, soon kept on call at the Forest of Literature Hall, and made recording officer in the Grand Marshal's office.

literal: Zhitui was clever, quick-witted, broadly learned, talented in debate, skilled at documents, and easy in reply; Zu Ting valued him greatly, put him in charge of the hall's affairs, and had him sign and judge papers.
idiomatic: Zhitui was clever, quick-witted, broadly learned, talented in debate, skilled at documents, and easy in reply; Zu Ting valued him greatly, put him in charge of the hall's affairs, and had him sign and judge papers.

literal: Soon he was promoted to attendant of direct communication and irregular cavalry, and shortly led the secretariat as secretary.
idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to attendant of direct communication and irregular cavalry, and shortly led the secretariat as secretary.

literal: Whenever the emperor had a request, he always sent a palace messenger to transmit the order; Zhitui received and announced it, and everyone in the hall took their cue from him.
idiomatic: Whenever the emperor had a request, he always sent a palace messenger to transmit the order; Zhitui received and announced it, and everyone in the hall took their cue from him.

literal: Every document submitted was sealed by him; he presented them at the Gate of Advancement to the Worthy and waited for a reply before they went out.
idiomatic: Every document submitted was sealed by him; he presented them at the Gate of Advancement to the Worthy and waited for a reply before they went out.

literal: He was also skilled at writing, supervised collation and copying, handled affairs diligently and swiftly, and was called competent in his post.
idiomatic: He was also skilled at writing, supervised collation and copying, handled affairs diligently and swiftly, and was called competent in his post.

literal: The emperor showed him great favor and regard beyond the usual; men of merit and power envied him and often wished to harm him.
idiomatic: The emperor showed him great favor and regard beyond the usual; men of merit and power envied him and often wished to harm him.

literal: When Cui Jishu and the others were about to remonstrate, Zhitui took urgent leave and returned home, and therefore did not join in the collective signature.
idiomatic: When Cui Jishu and the others were about to remonstrate, Zhitui took urgent leave and returned home, and therefore did not join in the collective signature.

literal: When the remonstrators were summoned, Zhitui was called in as well; on investigation his name was not among them, and only then did he escape disaster.
idiomatic: When the remonstrators were summoned, Zhitui was called in as well; on investigation his name was not among them, and only then did he escape disaster.

literal: Soon he was made gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
idiomatic: Soon he was made gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

literal: When the Zhou army took Jinyang, the emperor rode back to Ye in light armor; in desperate straits he had no plan to follow; Zhitui, through the eunuch attendant Deng Changyong, advanced a plan to flee to Chen, and urged recruiting more than a thousand Wu men as a personal guard, taking the Qing and Xu route together to throw themselves on Chen.
idiomatic: When the Zhou army took Jinyang, the emperor rode back to Ye in light armor; in desperate straits he had no plan to follow; Zhitui, through the eunuch attendant Deng Changyong, advanced a plan to flee to Chen, and urged recruiting more than a thousand Wu men as a personal guard, taking the Qing and Xu route together to throw themselves on Chen.

literal: The emperor was much inclined to accept it and told the chief minister Gao Anagong and the others.
idiomatic: The emperor was much inclined to accept it and told the chief minister Gao Anagong and the others.

literal: Anagong did not wish to enter Chen and said the Wu men were hard to trust and need not be recruited.
idiomatic: Anagong did not wish to enter Chen and said the Wu men were hard to trust and need not be recruited.

literal: He urged the emperor to send heavy treasures to Qing province and for the time being hold the land of the Three Qi; if it could not be kept, then cross the sea south to escape.
idiomatic: He urged the emperor to send heavy treasures to Qing province and for the time being hold the land of the Three Qi; if it could not be kept, then cross the sea south to escape.

literal: Though they did not follow Zhitui's plan, they still made him governor of Pingyuan and ordered him to guard the river crossing.
idiomatic: Though they did not follow Zhitui's plan, they still made him governor of Pingyuan and ordered him to guard the river crossing.

literal: When Qi fell he entered Zhou and, at the end of the Great Elephant era, was a senior scholar in the Censorate.
idiomatic: When Qi fell he entered Zhou and, at the end of the Great Elephant era, was a senior scholar in the Censorate.

literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui the heir summoned him as an academician and treated him with great ceremony.
idiomatic: In the Kaihuang era of Sui the heir summoned him as academician and treated him with great ceremony and weight.

literal: Before long he died of illness.
idiomatic: Before long he died of illness.

literal: He left thirty juan of writings and compiled twenty chapters of Family Instructions, both of which circulated in the world.
idiomatic: He left thirty juan of writings and compiled twenty chapters of Family Instructions, both of which circulated in the world.
